cands.name: Gus Michael Bilirakis
cands.bio: Republican U.S. Representative since 2007 (son of former Rep. Michael Bilirakis). Former probate and estate-planning lawyer; Florida House member for District 48, 1998-2006. Energy and Commerce Committee member; chaired its Innovation, Data, and Commerce subcommittee in the 118th Congress.
cands.local_ties: Born in Gainesville, raised in Tarpon Springs; lives in Palm Harbor (Pinellas County) per Wikipedia. The new 2026 District 12 covers parts of Pasco and Hillsborough counties (WUSF).

record.text: Energy and Commerce Committee (subcommittees on Communications and Technology, Health, and Innovation, Data, and Commerce, which he chaired in the 118th Congress); co-chair of the Congressional Military Veterans Caucus and the Congressional Caucus on Hellenic Issues.
Served in the Florida House (District 48) 1998-2006 before succeeding his father in Congress.

money_notes.text: Endorsed by AIPAC, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and the Associated Builders and Contractors Florida Gulf Coast Chapter (per the Wikipedia 2026 Florida House election page, which cites a U.S. Chamber release dated July 28, 2026 and Florida Politics).
Wikipedia reports $2,000 in direct contributions from the NRA Political Victory Fund in 2015-2016 (citing CNN, Feb. 2018). Older figure; not a current-cycle total.

controversies.text: October 2018 campaign ad credited him with the 'INTERDICT Act' opioid law; Fox News and the Tampa Bay Times reported he was neither its sponsor nor among its 18 co-sponsors (as summarized on Wikipedia; underlying articles not opened).

February 2017 Pasco town hall: CNN reported he nodded while a local party speaker repeated a 'death panels' claim about the ACA; he later told CNN the board exists and that he voted to repeal it (as summarized on Wikipedia).

endorsements.text: Donald Trump (endorsed Nov. 2025); U.S. Chamber of Commerce; AIPAC; Associated Builders and Contractors Florida Gulf Coast Chapter; Hillsborough Sheriff Chad Chronister and Pasco Sheriff Chris Nocco (Aug. 2026). Per Wikipedia's endorsement lists citing Florida Politics and the Chamber.

owner_sources.title: As Expected, A Hearing On Kids Online Safety Becomes A Blueprint For Digital ID
owner_sources.says: Per the search listing/excerpt only (page returned HTTP 403 to my fetch): the piece covers a House hearing on kids' online-safety bills that Bilirakis chaired and frames the bills as a path to digital ID. Not fact-checked.

cands.gaps: Current-cycle donor/outside-spending details not found (FEC totals handled separately). Underlying news articles for the controversies were not opened; sourced via Wikipedia. Infowars page blocked, so owner-source 'says' is from the search excerpt.

Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

cands.name: Kimberly Overman
cands.bio: Democratic nominee. Certified financial planner, small-business owner and former Hillsborough County commissioner (not Pinellas). Originally ran in the old District 15; moved to District 12 after the 2026 redistricting. Won the Aug. 18 primary with 52.7%.
cands.local_ties: Former Hillsborough County commissioner; campaign office at 4610 N Central Ave, Tampa. Residence not stated in sources reviewed.

record.text: Served on the Hillsborough County Board of County Commissioners (exact years not stated on her campaign site; she is described as a 'former' commissioner).
Moved her congressional bid from CD 15 to CD 12 after the May 2026 map change (Florida Politics headline cited on Wikipedia and in the Hernando Sun per her site).

money_notes.text: WUSF reported that primary opponent Darren McAuley had spent more than $728,000 as of July 29, roughly four times Overman's spending; Overman had netted over $186,000. These are primary-period figures.

endorsements.text: Listed on her campaign site: La Gaceta, End Citizens United, Brady PAC, West Central Florida Labor Council (AFL-CIO), Feminist Majority, Equality Florida, Moms Demand Action, National Women's Political Caucus, Emgage Action, Democratic Progressive Caucus of Florida, among others. (The site notes some labels may not match their linked pages.)
Post-primary: Rep. Suzan DelBene and DNC Chair Ken Martin (per Wikipedia citing Florida Politics).

cands.gaps: No county commission roll-call votes found or opened (votes omitted). Years of service and residence not verified. No controversies found in sources reviewed.
